question: When are faculties described as dissolved or without faculties?
premises: At great dissolution the faculties are broken and dissolved.
At creation they are not yet produced and remain dependent on will.
In that condition they are again called without faculties, and the same applies to their effects.
inference: The absence or latency of faculties is explained by cosmic dissolution, pre-creation latency, and dependence on divine will.
uncertainties: The verse compresses several temporal states into a single classificatory statement.
plain_english: At the great dissolution they are broken and dissolved; at creation they are not yet produced. Dependent on will, they are again called without faculties, and the same is true of their effects.
